tool_arguments.query: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI revenue Q2 FY2027 fiscal quarter

events.content: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI revenue Q2 FY2027 fiscal quarter

Oracle has not yet reported OCI (Cloud Infrastructure/IaaS) revenue for Q2 FY2027, the quarter ending November 30, 2026; its next earnings release is expected in mid-December 2026. [[1, 2]] 

Oracle’s Q2 FY2027 guidance is for **total cloud revenue**—OCI plus SaaS—to grow **65%–71% year over year in U.S. dollars**, rather than providing a standalone OCI-revenue dollar forecast. [[3]] 

For reference, OCI revenue in Q1 FY2027 was **$7.4 billion**, up **121% year over year**. [[3]]

Sources:

tool_arguments.query: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI remaining performance obligations RPO AI contracts FY2027

events.content: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI remaining performance obligations RPO AI contracts FY2027

**Oracle’s FY2027 AI-cloud/RPO position:** At the end of fiscal Q1 2027 (August 31, 2026), Oracle reported **$664 billion of remaining performance obligations (RPO)**, up **$209 billion year over year**. [[1]] 

Oracle said it booked **more than $30 billion of additional AI-cloud contracts** during the quarter, as demand for AI training and inference services continued to exceed available supply. [[1]] 

OCI/IaaS revenue was **$7.4 billion in Q1 FY2027**, up **121% year over year**; combined cloud revenue (IaaS plus SaaS) was **$11.6 billion**, up **62%**. [[1]] 

For conversion timing, Oracle’s Q1 FY2027 filing indicates approximately **13%** of RPO—about **$86 billion**—is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months, while approximately **50%** is expected within 36 months. [[2]] 

The important analytical caveat is that RPO is contracted, unrecognized revenue rather than OCI revenue guidance, and Oracle does not disclose the portion of the $664 billion backlog attributable specifically to OCI or to individual AI customers. [[2]] 

For full FY2027, Oracle guided to at least **$90 billion of total revenue** and **$8.10 of non-GAAP EPS**; it did not provide a standalone full-year OCI revenue target in the cited earnings release. [[1]] 

Oracle also stated that the structure of the new AI contracts creates **no incremental impact on its capital-raising plans**, suggesting a material role for prepayment, customer-supplied hardware, or other capital-light contract structures rather than Oracle solely funding all incremental compute capacity. [[1]]

Sources:
[S2.1] Oracle Announces Q1 Results Driven by Triple Digit Growth in Cloud Infrastructure Revenues — https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/q1fy27-earnings-release-2026-09-10/
[S2.2] Oracle Q1: Half of $664B RPO Expected as Revenue in 3 Years — https://financefeeds.com/oracle-q1-fy27-rpo-664-billion-36-month-conversion/

tool_arguments.summary:
Based on Oracle's Q1 FY2027 earnings release (period ending August 31, 2026):

- **OCI revenue**: $7.4 billion, up 121% year over year (S1.3).
- **Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO)**: $664 billion total at quarter-end, up $209 billion YoY; more than $30 billion of additional AI-cloud contracts were booked during the quarter (S2.1).
- **RPO conversion**: ~$86 billion (13% of RPO) expected to be recognized in the next 12 months; ~50% expected within 36 months (S2.2).

Note: Oracle does not break out OCI-specific RPO or AI-attributable RPO separately; the figures above reflect total company cloud and AI contract activity as reported in the filings.
